summary: Renders SOP line segments, edges, points, dots, and vectors with flat shading, distance-based width/color controls, and configurable caps and joints.

key_params.name: linetype
key_params.note: Line, point, vector, or related drawing mode

key_params.name: nearwidth
key_params.note: Width at near distance for rolloff models

key_params.name: farwidth
key_params.note: Width at far distance for rolloff models

key_params.name: startcappullback
key_params.note: Pull back the start cap along the line

key_concepts: Line MAT renders 3D line segments, polygon edges, dots, points, and per-point vectors rather than filled shaded surfaces.
The shader is flat shaded, so line color and width are controlled by MAT parameters and attributes instead of scene lighting.
Line width is resolution-independent by default and can also be driven by SOP point attributes such as width or pscale.
Depth interpolation, near/far rolloff, and FOV/Ortho Width behavior determine whether line width and color remain visually stable through camera changes.
Caps, hinges, arrows, points, and vector controls are part of the material shape, so they affect actual rendered extents and joins.
common_gotchas: Line MAT is flat shaded and is not affected by scene lights like Phong or PBR materials.
Width and color can vary with distance to camera; check rolloff settings before assuming constant screen-space width.
Caps and hinges affect visual length and joins, so they matter for arrows, vectors, and dense line fields.
The input geometry must contain suitable lines, edges, points, or vectors for the selected rendering mode.
